pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected. I couldn't run the suite (vitest not installed), so this rests on reading.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' only when starred. 'AC-2' asserts the exact list [First item, ★ Second item, Third item].
The starred view uses WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and expects them in id order with status 200.
'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order, with the star shown.
'AC-5' checks the Starred only link on / and the All items link on the starred view.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) guards against __proto__. 'AC-6' checks Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>.
traffic/routes.json now contains /?show=starred. 'AC-7' asserts that. The check script and traffic worker handle the query string correctly.

findings.what: The fakeApp now records the query string and keys answers by path plus search, but no traffic test uses a route with a query. The change is unexercised, so nothing shows the traffic worker's check() handles a query route.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that stubs ROUTES, or use a route like /?show=starred, and asserts the fake app saw the query and that a failure on it is reported.

findings.what: The check now accepts a query string, but its error text still says 'array of paths starting with "/"', and the README doesn't say routes may carry a query.
findings.fix: Update the message and the README line to say a path may include a query string.

lenses.note: The spec exists with a go dated 2026-10-12. Decisions are followed: starred items stay in id order, and the view is a query parameter.

All 7 acceptance items and all 4 state rows have tests. No commit edits the spec after the go; the spec arrives in the same diff as the code. Nothing extra was added beyond the CHECK constraint, which is harmless.
Tests assert behaviour. I couldn't run them because vitest isn't installed. No tests were deleted or loosened. One low finding on the unused fakeApp change.
The README is updated. One low finding on the stale wording about routes.
The show parameter is validated with hasOwn, so __proto__ and similar keys are rejected. Titles are escaped. No defects found.
The query value is only used as a lookup key in a fixed map, and the SQL is built from static strings. No injection path found.
The diff touches only the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js and adds no UI or style files.

The title and body match the diff: the migration, ★, the show values with 400, the routes.json entry, the traffic-check relaxation and the fakeApp change. The body says the check refuses spaces and #; the new shell tests cover both.
